properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Wish #38 from the dev_storyflow agent, 2026-09-07 (peer feedback lines 7299-7303), in their words: "nothing in reflow2 knows that a verification named 'the page' was proven at 'the route'. Wish (#38): let a Verification carry a `surface` (route / page / store / prompt) so a pass at one surface cannot silently stand for the one above it."

WHAT HAPPENED TO THEM, which is the part worth keeping. A check named "the Fallacies page can show a fallacy" had been set passing on a ROUTE measurement the day before. Walking the actual page showed zero. They caught it themselves, moved the check back to failing with the correction in its findings, and let a new page-level check supersede it. So the design corrected itself through a human noticing, and nothing in the loop could have asked.

OPTIONS, unranked:
(a) A new `surface` enum on Verification, values as they proposed. Says the thing directly, and every project has different surfaces — route/page/store/prompt is a web vocabulary, and a beamline or a spacecraft has none of those.
(b) A free-text `surface` string. Portable across domains, unrankable by anything, so it can be recorded and never read.
(c) Reuse `Verification.level`, which already exists for exactly this shape of question. Costs no vocabulary at all.
(d) Do nothing; the reporter's own correction worked, and the record now shows it.

THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT IS ALREADY MEASURED IN THIS DESIGN AND IT IS THE STRONGEST THING HERE. Verification.level exists today and NOTHING READS IT — fact:defect-realized-was-claimed-at-unit-and-nothing-in-the-loop-asked records that a capability was claimed realized on a unit-level check and no gap, no loop_status line and no tool asked "green where?". Adding a second unread property beside the first would make the design say more and know no more. By fact:vocabulary-needs-three-legs this idea needs a typed field AND an instruction AND a detector that notices the mismatch; the wish as written asks only for the first leg, which is the leg this project already has.

SO THE REAL QUESTION IS NOT surface-versus-nothing. It is whether a claim of a pass at one granularity, where the check's own NAME claims another, is a thing a detector can see — and if it is, whether `level` is already the place to see it.
properties.name: OPEN — should a Verification say WHICH SURFACE it was proven at (route / page / store / prompt), so a pass one layer down cannot stand for the layer above it?
properties.rationale: Recorded rather than built because the obvious form of it repeats a known failure. The reporter's problem is real and they demonstrated it on themselves, but the vocabulary they ask for already has a sibling in the schema that no computation reads, so building the field first would produce the same silence one property along. What would settle it is a detector: given a check whose name asserts one surface and whose evidence was taken at another, can anything notice without a human walking the page? If yes, the property earns its place; if no, neither property does.
